description: The Rudder Cloud control plane: HTTP traffic and errors, sockets to homes and clients, its own event loop and memory, and each home's heartbeat.

panels.description: HTTP requests the control plane served, all routes.
panels.title: Requests per second

panels.description: 95th percentile request time over the last 5 minutes. Red usually means the event loop is blocked (see Event loop delay) or the database is slow.
panels.title: Latency p95

panels.description: Share of requests that failed with a server error over the last 5 minutes. Red means users are seeing failures: find the route in the Routes table and check the control plane logs.
panels.title: 5xx share

panels.description: Homes whose last heartbeat is more than 2 minutes old (they send one every 30 seconds). Amber means a supervisor is stuck or a home died without the control plane noticing: open it from the Homes table below.
panels.title: Stale heartbeats

panels.description: Home supervisors with an open control socket. Lower than the running homes means some homes cannot be reached and their terminals show "reconnecting".
panels.title: Home sockets

panels.description: Terminals, phones and browsers connected to the control plane.
panels.title: Client sockets

panels.description: How late the control plane's event loop runs at the 99th percentile. It relays every terminal; red means everyone's typing lags. Check process memory and recent deploys.
panels.title: Event loop p99

panels.description: Resident memory of the control plane process. A steady climb across days is a leak; restart during a quiet window and report it.
panels.title: Memory RSS

panels.description: Request rate per route (ids in paths are replaced by :id). A route that jumps on its own is usually a client retrying in a loop.
panels.title: Requests per second by route

panels.description: Request time percentiles over all routes. p99 far above p95 means a few slow routes; find them in the Routes table.
panels.title: Latency

panels.description: Server errors per second by route. Any steady rate means a route is broken for someone: check the control plane logs for that route.
panels.title: 5xx responses per second

panels.description: Server errors as a share of all requests. Above the red line users are seeing failures on a meaningful share of requests.
panels.title: 5xx share of requests

panels.description: Every route over the last 5 minutes, busiest first. Amber and red cells are slow or failing routes: check the control plane logs for that route.
panels.title: Routes

panels.description: Open sockets: home-control is one per connected home supervisor, client is attached terminals, phones and browsers, worker is task workers. A sudden drop in home-control is many homes reconnecting at once, usually a control plane restart.
panels.title: WebSocket connections by role

panels.description: Homes the control plane knows, by state, largest first. Failed homes need someone to look at the Fly machine.
panels.title: Homes by state

panels.description: Sails the control plane knows, by state, largest first. Many queued sails with few running means workers are not starting.
panels.title: Sails by state

panels.description: How late the control plane's event loop runs. Above the amber line terminal input lags for everyone; above the red line sockets start timing out.
panels.title: Event loop delay

panels.description: Resident memory (rss) and JavaScript heap of the control plane process. Heap climbing with rss is a leak in our code; rss climbing alone is native buffers (sockets, SQLite).
panels.title: Process memory

panels.description: Every home the control plane tracks, stalest heartbeat first. Red heartbeat age or Disconnected means a running home's users cannot reach it. Stopped and paused homes do not heartbeat; Control shows their state and the age reads -. Click a home to open its page.

properties.value: The control plane's view: Connected or Disconnected while the home is running, otherwise the home's state (a stopped home is quiet on purpose)

targets.expr: (max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_control_connected_ratio) and on (rudder_home_id) max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="running"} == 1)) or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="queued"} == 1) * 2 or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="paused"} == 1) * 3 or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="stopped"} == 1) * 4 or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="failed"} == 1) * 5 or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_state{state="running"} == 1) * 6 or max by (rudder_home_id) (rudder_control_home_control_connected_ratio)

panels.title: Home heartbeats

panels.description: Control socket closes per home in 5 minute buckets. Many homes at the same moment is the control plane (a deploy or a stall); one home again and again is that home (open it from the table).
panels.title: Home disconnects, per 5 minutes

panels.description: Burst build pool machines across all homes. Leased builders are running someone's build; idle ones keep their caches and stop themselves after a few quiet minutes. Failed or destroying builders that stay for more than a few minutes mean Fly calls are failing. Empty while RUDDER_BUILDERS is off.
panels.title: Builders by state

panels.description: rudder-burst lease requests by outcome. Cold starts wait for a machine to start or be created; busy means every builder of that home was leased (the client waits and retries), so steady busy bars mean the per-home maximum is too low.
panels.title: Builder lease requests, per 5 minutes
